newsitem.title: FRANCE: Protest after Frenchman killed defending brother.
newsitem.headline: Protest after Frenchman killed defending brother.

text.p: Several hundred people marched in protest before city hall in the southern French city of Marseille on Sunday against the murder of a man who defended his mentally handicapped brother against youths pestering him.
Three of the suspected killers, between 15 and 17 years old, have been held in police custody since Friday after Yves Radion, 35, was stabbed and beaten to death on Wednesday evening.
Radion, a father of four children, was killed after he accused a group of local youths of regularly pestering his handicapped younger brother in a poor Marseille neighbourhood.
The protest was briefly marred by a clash with local leaders of the anti-immigrant National Front who tried to join the march to dramatise their calls for tougher measures against crime.

The National Front held a large protest rally last year after a local teenager was killed by a youth of Arab origin and has since held law-and-order demonstrations no matter whether the criminals were of French or foreign background.
Police said the suspects were French citizens but did not reveal their names because they are minors.
Radion's wife and in-laws are of North African origin and several of them insisted the National Front activists leave the protest immediately.
"We came here to see that what has occurred does not happen to others," a brother-in-law called out to the crowd. "Whoever is here for racist reasons should leave!"
Jean-Claude Gaudin, the centrist mayor of Marseille, met Radion's relatives after the march and promised to help them move out of the neighbourhood.
